passages.text: On the twenty-fourth day of the same month, the Israelites gathered together, fasting and wearing sackcloth, with dust on their heads.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites had returned from exile.
On the twenty-fourth day of that month, they gathered together.
They fasted.
They wore sackcloth.
They put dust on their heads.
passages.original: וּבְיוֹם֩ עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֜ה לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַזֶּ֗ה נֶאֶסְפ֤וּ בְנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בְּצ֣וֹם וּבְשַׂקִּ֔ים וַאֲדָמָ֖ה עֲלֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: Those of Israelite descent separated themselves from all the foreigners, and they stood and confessed their sins and the iniquities of their fathers.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites were the descendants of Israel.
They separated themselves from all foreigners.
They stood up.
They confessed their own sins.
They confessed the sins of their fathers.
passages.original: וַיִּבָּֽדְלוּ֙ זֶ֣רַע יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מִכֹּ֖ל בְּנֵ֣י נֵכָ֑ר וַיַּעַמְד֗וּ וַיִּתְוַדּוּ֙ עַל־ חַטֹּ֣אתֵיהֶ֔ם וַעֲוֺנ֖וֹת אֲבֹתֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: While they stood in their places, they read from the Book of the Law of the LORD their God for a quarter of the day, and they spent another quarter of the day in confession and worship of the LORD their God.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites gathered together.
They stood in their places.
They read from the Book of the Law of the LORD their God.
They read for a quarter of the day.
They confessed their sins for another quarter of the day.
They worshiped the LORD their God.
passages.original: וַיָּק֙וּמוּ֙ עַל־ עָמְדָ֔ם וַֽיִּקְרְא֗וּ בְּסֵ֨פֶר תּוֹרַ֧ת יְהוָ֛ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֖ם רְבִעִ֣ית הַיּ֑וֹם וּרְבִעִית֙ מִתְוַדִּ֣ים וּמִֽשְׁתַּחֲוִ֔ים לַיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶֽם׃פ

passages.text: And the Levites—Jeshua, Bani, Kadmiel, Shebaniah, Bunni, Sherebiah, Bani, and Chenani—stood on the raised platform and cried out in a loud voice to the LORD their God.
passages.sermon:
The Levites were leaders among the people of Israel.
Their names were Jeshua, Bani, Kadmiel, Shebaniah, Bunni, Sherebiah, Bani, and Chenani.
They stood on a raised platform.
They cried out with a loud voice.
They called to the LORD, who is their God.
passages.original: וַיָּ֜קָם עַֽל־ מַֽעֲלֵ֣ה הַלְוִיִּ֗ם יֵשׁ֨וּעַ וּבָנִ֜י קַדְמִיאֵ֧ל שְׁבַנְיָ֛ה בֻּנִּ֥י שֵׁרֵבְיָ֖ה בָּנִ֣י כְנָ֑נִי וַֽיִּזְעֲקוּ֙ בְּק֣וֹל גָּד֔וֹל אֶל־ יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: Then the Levites—Jeshua, Kadmiel, Bani, Hashabneiah, Sherebiah, Hodiah, Shebaniah, and Pethahiah—said, “Stand up and bless the LORD your God from everlasting to everlasting: Blessed be Your glorious name, and may it be exalted above all blessing and praise.
passages.sermon:
The Levites spoke to the people.
The Levites were Jeshua, Kadmiel, Bani, Hashabneiah, Sherebiah, Hodiah, Shebaniah, and Pethahiah.
They said, "Stand up."
They said, "Bless the LORD your God."
The LORD is your God forever.
The LORD is your God from everlasting to everlasting.
Bless the glorious name of the LORD.
The name of the LORD is above every blessing.
The name of the LORD is above every praise.
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ הַלְוִיִּ֡ם יֵשׁ֣וּעַ וְ֠קַדְמִיאֵל בָּנִ֨י חֲשַׁבְנְיָ֜ה שֵׁרֵֽבְיָ֤ה הֽוֹדִיָּה֙ שְׁבַנְיָ֣ה פְתַֽחְיָ֔ה ק֗וּמוּ בָּרֲכוּ֙ אֶת־ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֔ם מִן־ הָעוֹלָ֖ם עַד־ הָעוֹלָ֑ם וִיבָֽרְכוּ֙ שֵׁ֣ם כְּבוֹדֶ֔ךָ וּמְרוֹמַ֥ם עַל־ כָּל־ בְּרָכָ֖ה וּתְהִלָּֽה׃

passages.text: You alone are the LORD. You created the heavens, the highest heavens with all their host, the earth and all that is on it, the seas and all that is in them. You give life to all things, and the host of heaven worships You.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God alone.
He alone exists as the LORD.
He created the heavens.
He made the highest heavens.
He made all the hosts of heaven.
He created the earth.
He made everything on the earth.
He created the seas.
He made everything in the seas.
He gives life to all things.
The host of heaven worships Him.
passages.original: אַתָּה־ ה֣וּא יְהוָה֮ לְבַדֶּךָ֒ אַתְּ עָשִׂ֡יתָ אֶֽת־ הַשָּׁמַיִם֩ שְׁמֵ֨י הַשָּׁמַ֜יִם וְכָל־ צְבָאָ֗ם הָאָ֜רֶץ וְכָל־ אֲשֶׁ֤ר עָלֶ֙יהָ֙ הַיַּמִּים֙ וְכָל־ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּהֶ֔ם וְאַתָּ֖ה מְחַיֶּ֣ה אֶת־ כֻּלָּ֑ם וּצְבָ֥א הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם לְךָ֥ מִשְׁתַּחֲוִֽים׃

passages.text: You are the LORD, the God who chose Abram, who brought him out of Ur of the Chaldeans and gave him the name Abraham.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God alone.
The LORD chose Abram.
The LORD brought Abram out of Ur of the Chaldeans.
The LORD gave Abram a new name.
The LORD called him Abraham.
passages.original: אַתָּה־ הוּא֙ יְהוָ֣ה הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר בָּחַ֙רְתָּ֙ בְּאַבְרָ֔ם וְהוֹצֵאת֖וֹ מֵא֣וּר כַּשְׂדִּ֑ים וְשַׂ֥מְתָּ שְּׁמ֖וֹ אַבְרָהָֽם׃

passages.text: You found his heart faithful before You, and made a covenant with him to give the land of the Canaanites and Hittites, of the Amorites and Perizzites, of the Jebusites and Girgashites— to give it to his descendants. You have kept Your promise, because You are righteous.
passages.sermon:
God looked at Abraham’s heart.
God saw that Abraham was faithful.
God made a covenant with Abraham.
God promised to give Abraham land.
This land belonged to the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Jebusites, and Girgashites.
God promised to give this land to Abraham’s descendants.
God kept His promise.
God is righteous.
passages.original: וּמָצָ֣אתָ אֶת־ לְבָבוֹ֮ נֶאֱמָ֣ן לְפָנֶיךָ֒ וְכָר֨וֹת עִמּ֜וֹ הַבְּרִ֗ית לָתֵ֡ת אֶת־ אֶרֶץ֩ הַכְּנַעֲנִ֨י הַחִתִּ֜י הָאֱמֹרִ֧י וְהַפְּרִזִּ֛י וְהַיְבוּסִ֥י וְהַגִּרְגָּשִׁ֖י לָתֵ֣ת לְזַרְע֑וֹ וַתָּ֙קֶם֙ אֶת־ דְּבָרֶ֔יךָ כִּ֥י צַדִּ֖יק אָֽתָּה׃

passages.text: You saw the affliction of our fathers in Egypt; You heard their cry at the Red Sea.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
The LORD watched over our ancestors.
Our ancestors suffered in Egypt.
The LORD saw their suffering.
Our ancestors cried out at the Red Sea.
The LORD heard their cry.
passages.original: וַתֵּ֛רֶא אֶת־ עֳנִ֥י אֲבֹתֵ֖ינוּ בְּמִצְרָ֑יִם וְאֶת־ זַעֲקָתָ֥ם שָׁמַ֖עְתָּ עַל־ יַם־ סֽוּף׃

passages.text: You performed signs and wonders against Pharaoh, all his officials, and all the people of his land, for You knew they had acted with arrogance against our fathers. You made a name for Yourself that endures to this day.
passages.sermon:
God acted with power in Egypt.
God performed signs and wonders.
God did these things against Pharaoh.
God did these things against all Pharaoh’s officials.
God did these things against all the people of Pharaoh’s land.
God knew that Pharaoh and his people acted with arrogance against our fathers.
God made a name for Himself.
God’s name remains great to this day.
passages.original: וַ֠תִּתֵּן אֹתֹ֨ת וּמֹֽפְתִ֜ים בְּפַרְעֹ֤ה וּבְכָל־ עֲבָדָיו֙ וּבְכָל־ עַ֣ם אַרְצ֔וֹ כִּ֣י יָדַ֔עְתָּ כִּ֥י הֵזִ֖ידוּ עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם וַתַּֽעַשׂ־ לְךָ֥ שֵׁ֖ם כְּהַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: You divided the sea before them, and they crossed through it on dry ground. You hurled their pursuers into the depths like a stone into raging waters.
passages.sermon:
God acted with great power for the Israelites.
God divided the sea in front of the Israelites.
The Israelites walked through the sea on dry ground.
God threw the Egyptians, who chased the Israelites, into the deep waters.
The Egyptians sank like a stone in strong, rushing water.
passages.original: וְהַיָּם֙ בָּקַ֣עְתָּ לִפְנֵיהֶ֔ם וַיַּֽעַבְר֥וּ בְתוֹךְ־ הַיָּ֖ם בַּיַּבָּשָׁ֑ה וְֽאֶת־ רֹ֨דְפֵיהֶ֜ם הִשְׁלַ֧כְתָּ בִמְצוֹלֹ֛ת כְּמוֹ־ אֶ֖בֶן בְּמַ֥יִם עַזִּֽים׃

passages.text: You led them with a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night, to light for them the way in which they should travel.
passages.sermon:
God led the Israelites.
He used a pillar of cloud during the day.
He used a pillar of fire at night.
God showed them the way to travel.
The pillar of fire gave them light at night.
The pillars guided them on their journey.
passages.original: וּבְעַמּ֣וּד עָנָ֔ן הִנְחִיתָ֖ם יוֹמָ֑ם וּבְעַמּ֥וּד אֵשׁ֙ לַ֔יְלָה לְהָאִ֣יר לָהֶ֔ם אֶת־ הַדֶּ֖רֶךְ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יֵֽלְכוּ־ בָֽהּ׃

passages.text: You came down on Mount Sinai and spoke with them from heaven. You gave them just ordinances, true laws, and good statutes and commandments.
passages.sermon:
God came down on Mount Sinai.
God spoke with the people from heaven.
God gave the people just ordinances.
God gave the people true laws.
God gave the people good statutes.
God gave the people good commandments.
passages.original: וְעַ֤ל הַר־ סִינַי֙ יָרַ֔דְתָּ וְדַבֵּ֥ר עִמָּהֶ֖ם מִשָּׁמָ֑יִם וַתִּתֵּ֨ן לָהֶ֜ם מִשְׁפָּטִ֤ים יְשָׁרִים֙ וְתוֹר֣וֹת אֱמֶ֔ת חֻקִּ֥ים וּמִצְוֺ֖ת טוֹבִֽים׃

passages.text: You revealed to them Your holy Sabbath and gave them commandments and statutes and laws through Your servant Moses.
passages.sermon:
God revealed His holy Sabbath to the people of Israel.
God gave them commandments.
God gave them statutes.
God gave them laws.
God gave these through Moses, His servant.
passages.original: וְאֶת־ שַׁבַּ֥ת קָדְשְׁךָ֖ הוֹדַ֣עַתָ לָהֶ֑ם וּמִצְו֤וֹת וְחֻקִּים֙ וְתוֹרָ֔ה צִוִּ֣יתָ לָהֶ֔ם בְּיַ֖ד מֹשֶׁ֥ה עַבְדֶּֽךָ׃

passages.text: In their hunger You gave them bread from heaven; in their thirst You brought them water from the rock. You told them to go in and possess the land which You had sworn to give them.
passages.sermon:
God cared for the Israelites in the wilderness.
They were hungry.
God gave them bread from heaven.
They were thirsty.
God brought them water from a rock.
God told the Israelites to enter the land.
God had promised to give them this land.
God had sworn to give them this land.
passages.original: וְ֠לֶחֶם מִשָּׁמַ֜יִם נָתַ֤תָּה לָהֶם֙ לִרְעָבָ֔ם וּמַ֗יִם מִסֶּ֛לַע הוֹצֵ֥אתָ לָהֶ֖ם לִצְמָאָ֑ם וַתֹּ֣אמֶר לָהֶ֗ם לָבוֹא֙ לָרֶ֣שֶׁת אֶת־ הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־ נָשָׂ֥אתָ אֶת־ יָדְךָ֖ לָתֵ֥ת לָהֶֽם׃

passages.text: But they and our fathers became arrogant and stiff-necked and did not obey Your commandments.
passages.sermon:
The people acted arrogantly.
Our fathers also acted arrogantly.
They became stubborn.
They refused to listen.
They did not obey Your commandments.
passages.original: וְהֵ֥ם וַאֲבֹתֵ֖ינוּ הֵזִ֑ידוּ וַיַּקְשׁוּ֙ אֶת־ עָרְפָּ֔ם וְלֹ֥א שָׁמְע֖וּ אֶל־ מִצְוֺתֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: They refused to listen and failed to remember the wonders You performed among them. They stiffened their necks and appointed a leader to return them to their bondage in Egypt. But You are a forgiving God, gracious and compassionate, slow to anger and rich in loving devotion, and You did not forsake them.
passages.sermon:
The people refused to listen.
They did not remember the wonders You performed among them.
They became stubborn.
They chose a leader to take them back to slavery in Egypt.
You are a forgiving God.
You are gracious and compassionate.
You are slow to anger.
You are rich in loving devotion.
You did not abandon them.
passages.original: וַיְמָאֲנ֣וּ לִשְׁמֹ֗עַ וְלֹא־ זָכְר֤וּ נִפְלְאֹתֶ֙יךָ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֣יתָ עִמָּהֶ֔ם וַיַּקְשׁוּ֙ אֶת־ עָרְפָּ֔ם וַיִּתְּנוּ־ רֹ֛אשׁ לָשׁ֥וּב לְעַבְדֻתָ֖ם בְּמִרְיָ֑ם וְאַתָּה֩ אֱל֨וֹהַּ סְלִיח֜וֹת חַנּ֧וּן וְרַח֛וּם אֶֽרֶךְ־ אַפַּ֥יִם וְרַב־ וְחֶסֶד וְלֹ֥א עֲזַבְתָּֽם׃

passages.text: Even when they cast for themselves an image of a calf and said, ‘This is your God who brought you up out of Egypt,’ and when they committed terrible blasphemies, You in Your great compassion did not forsake them in the wilderness. By day the pillar of cloud never turned away from guiding them on their path; and by the night the pillar of fire illuminated the way they should go.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites made for themselves a calf from metal.
They said, “This is your God who brought you out of Egypt.”
They committed great blasphemies.
God showed great compassion.
God did not abandon the Israelites in the wilderness.
During the day, the pillar of cloud stayed with them.
The pillar of cloud guided them on their way.
At night, the pillar of fire shone for them.
The pillar of fire showed them the way they should go.
passages.original: אַ֗ף כִּֽי־ עָשׂ֤וּ לָהֶם֙ עֵ֣גֶל מַסֵּכָ֔ה וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ זֶ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶעֶלְךָ֖ מִמִּצְרָ֑יִם וַֽיַּעֲשׂ֔וּ נֶאָצ֖וֹת גְּדֹלֽוֹת׃ וְאַתָּה֙ בְּרַחֲמֶ֣יךָ הָֽרַבִּ֔ים לֹ֥א עֲזַבְתָּ֖ם בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר אֶת־ עַמּ֣וּד הֶ֠עָנָן לֹא־ סָ֨ר מֵעֲלֵיהֶ֤ם בְּיוֹמָם֙ לְהַנְחֹתָ֣ם בְּהַדֶּ֔רֶךְ וְאֶת־ עַמּ֨וּד הָאֵ֤שׁ בְּלַ֙יְלָה֙ לְהָאִ֣יר לָהֶ֔ם וְאֶת־ הַדֶּ֖רֶךְ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יֵֽלְכוּ־ בָֽהּ׃

passages.text: You gave Your good Spirit to instruct them. You did not withhold Your manna from their mouths, and You gave them water for their thirst.
passages.sermon:
God gave His good Spirit to the people of Israel.
God gave His Spirit to help them understand and learn.
God did not withhold manna from them.
God provided manna for them to eat.
God gave them water when they were thirsty.
passages.original: וְרוּחֲךָ֨ הַטּוֹבָ֔ה נָתַ֖תָּ לְהַשְׂכִּילָ֑ם וּמַנְךָ֙ לֹא־ מָנַ֣עְתָּ מִפִּיהֶ֔ם וּמַ֛יִם נָתַ֥תָּה לָהֶ֖ם לִצְמָאָֽם׃

passages.text: For forty years You sustained them in the wilderness, so that they lacked nothing. Their clothes did not wear out and their feet did not swell.
passages.sermon:
God cared for the Israelites in the wilderness for forty years.
God provided everything they needed.
The Israelites did not lack anything.
Their clothes did not wear out.
Their feet did not swell.
passages.original: וְאַרְבָּעִ֥ים שָׁנָ֛ה כִּלְכַּלְתָּ֥ם בַּמִּדְבָּ֖ר לֹ֣א חָסֵ֑רוּ שַׂלְמֹֽתֵיהֶם֙ לֹ֣א בָל֔וּ וְרַגְלֵיהֶ֖ם לֹ֥א בָצֵֽקוּ׃

passages.text: You gave them kingdoms and peoples and allotted to them every corner of the land. So they took the land of Sihon king of Heshbon and of Og king of Bashan.
passages.sermon:
God gave the Israelites kingdoms.
God gave the Israelites peoples.
God divided the land among the Israelites.
God gave the Israelites every part of the land.
The Israelites took the land of Sihon.
Sihon was king of Heshbon.
The Israelites took the land of Og.
Og was king of Bashan.
passages.original: וַתִּתֵּ֨ן לָהֶ֤ם מַמְלָכוֹת֙ וַעֲמָמִ֔ים וַֽתַּחְלְקֵ֖ם לְפֵאָ֑ה וַיִּֽירְשׁ֞וּ אֶת־ אֶ֣רֶץ סִיח֗וֹן וְאֶת־ אֶ֙רֶץ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ חֶשְׁבּ֔וֹן וְאֶת־ אֶ֖רֶץ ע֥וֹג מֶֽלֶךְ־ הַבָּשָֽׁן׃

passages.text: You multiplied their descendants like the stars of heaven and brought them to the land You had told their fathers to enter and possess.
passages.sermon:
God multiplied the descendants of Israel.
He made their numbers very great.
Their descendants became as many as the stars in the sky.
God brought these descendants to a special land.
God had promised this land to their fathers.
God told their fathers to enter and possess this land.
God fulfilled His promise by bringing their descendants there.
passages.original: וּבְנֵיהֶ֣ם הִרְבִּ֔יתָ כְּכֹכְבֵ֖י הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם וַתְּבִיאֵם֙ אֶל־ הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־ אָמַ֥רְתָּ לַאֲבֹתֵיהֶ֖ם לָב֥וֹא לָרָֽשֶׁת׃

passages.text: So their descendants went in and possessed the land; You subdued before them the Canaanites dwelling in the land. You delivered into their hands the kings and peoples of the land, to do with them as they wished.
passages.sermon:
God led the descendants of Israel into the land.
The descendants of Israel took possession of the land.
God made the Canaanites, who lived in the land, submit before the Israelites.
God gave the Canaanites into the hands of the Israelites.
God also gave the kings of the land into their hands.
God gave the peoples of the land into their hands.
The Israelites did with them as they wished.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֤אוּ הַבָּנִים֙ וַיִּֽירְשׁ֣וּ אֶת־ הָאָ֔רֶץ וַתַּכְנַ֨ע לִפְנֵיהֶ֜ם אֶת־ יֹשְׁבֵ֤י הָאָ֙רֶץ֙ הַכְּנַ֣עֲנִ֔ים וַֽתִּתְּנֵ֖ם בְּיָדָ֑ם וְאֶת־ מַלְכֵיהֶם֙ וְאֶת־ עַֽמְמֵ֣י הָאָ֔רֶץ לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת בָּהֶ֖ם כִּרְצוֹנָֽם׃

passages.text: They captured fortified cities and fertile land and took houses full of all goods, wells already dug, vineyards, olive groves, and fruit trees in abundance. So they ate and were filled; they grew fat and delighted in Your great goodness.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites captured strong cities.
They took fertile land.
They received houses filled with every good thing.
They found wells already dug.
They took vineyards.
They took olive groves.
They took many fruit trees.
They ate the food.
They became full.
They grew fat.
They enjoyed Your great goodness.
passages.original: וַֽיִּלְכְּד֞וּ עָרִ֣ים בְּצֻרוֹת֮ וַאֲדָמָ֣ה שְׁמֵנָה֒ וַיִּֽירְשׁ֡וּ בָּתִּ֣ים מְלֵֽאִים־ כָּל־ ט֠וּב בֹּר֨וֹת חֲצוּבִ֜ים כְּרָמִ֧ים וְזֵיתִ֛ים וְעֵ֥ץ מַאֲכָ֖ל לָרֹ֑ב וַיֹּאכְל֤וּ וַֽיִּשְׂבְּעוּ֙ וַיַּשְׁמִ֔ינוּ וַיִּֽתְעַדְּנ֖וּ בְּטוּבְךָ֥ הַגָּדֽוֹל׃

passages.text: But they were disobedient and rebelled against You; they flung Your law behind their backs. They killed Your prophets, who had admonished them to return to You. They committed terrible blasphemies.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites disobeyed God.
They rebelled against God.
They threw God's law behind their backs.
They killed God's prophets.
These prophets had warned them to return to God.
The Israelites committed terrible blasphemies.
passages.original: וַיַּמְר֨וּ וַֽיִּמְרְד֜וּ בָּ֗ךְ וַיַּשְׁלִ֤כוּ אֶת־ תּוֹרָֽתְךָ֙ אַחֲרֵ֣י גַוָּ֔ם וְאֶת־ נְבִיאֶ֣יךָ הָרָ֔גוּ אֲשֶׁר־ הֵעִ֥ידוּ בָ֖ם לַהֲשִׁיבָ֣ם אֵלֶ֑יךָ וַֽיַּעֲשׂ֔וּ נֶאָצ֖וֹת גְּדוֹלֹֽת׃

passages.text: So You delivered them into the hands of enemies who oppressed them, and in their time of distress they cried out to You. From heaven You heard them, and in Your great compassion You gave them deliverers who saved them from the hands of their enemies.
passages.sermon:
God dealt with the people of Israel.
They sinned and turned away from Him.
God gave them into the hands of their enemies.
Their enemies oppressed them.
The Israelites suffered in distress.
In their trouble, they cried out to God.
God heard them from heaven.
God showed them great compassion.
God gave them deliverers.
These deliverers saved the Israelites from their enemies.
passages.original: וַֽתִּתְּנֵם֙ בְּיַ֣ד צָֽרֵיהֶ֔ם וַיָּצֵ֖רוּ לָהֶ֑ם וּבְעֵ֤ת צָֽרָתָם֙ יִצְעֲק֣וּ אֵלֶ֔יךָ וְאַתָּה֙ מִשָּׁמַ֣יִם תִּשְׁמָ֔ע וּֽכְרַחֲמֶ֣יךָ הָֽרַבִּ֗ים תִּתֵּ֤ן לָהֶם֙ מֽוֹשִׁיעִ֔ים וְיוֹשִׁיע֖וּם מִיַּ֥ד צָרֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: But as soon as they had rest, they again did evil in Your sight. So You abandoned them to the hands of their enemies, who had dominion over them. When they cried out to You again, You heard from heaven, and You delivered them many times in Your compassion.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel found rest.
They quickly returned to doing evil before God.
God saw their evil.
God left them in the power of their enemies.
Their enemies ruled over them.
The people cried out to God again.
God heard them from heaven.
God saved them many times.
God acted because He is compassionate.
passages.original: וּכְנ֣וֹחַ לָהֶ֔ם יָשׁ֕וּבוּ לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת רַ֖ע לְפָנֶ֑יךָ וַתַּֽעַזְבֵ֞ם בְּיַ֤ד אֹֽיְבֵיהֶם֙ וַיִּרְדּ֣וּ בָהֶ֔ם וַיָּשׁ֙וּבוּ֙ וַיִּזְעָק֔וּךָ וְאַתָּ֞ה מִשָּׁמַ֧יִם תִּשְׁמַ֛ע וְתַצִּילֵ֥ם כְּֽרַחֲמֶ֖יךָ רַבּ֥וֹת עִתִּֽים׃

passages.text: You admonished them to turn back to Your law, but they were arrogant and disobeyed Your commandments. They sinned against Your ordinances, by which a man will live if he practices them. They stubbornly shrugged their shoulders; they stiffened their necks and would not obey.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the people of Israel.
God warned them to return to His law.
The people acted with pride.
They did not obey God's commandments.
They broke God's rules.
God's rules give life to those who follow them.
The people turned away from God.
They stubbornly refused to listen.
They made their necks stiff.
They would not obey God.
passages.original: וַתָּ֨עַד בָּהֶ֜ם לַהֲשִׁיבָ֣ם אֶל־ תּוֹרָתֶ֗ךָ וְהֵ֨מָּה הֵזִ֜ידוּ וְלֹא־ שָׁמְע֤וּ לְמִצְוֺתֶ֙יךָ֙ וּבְמִשְׁפָּטֶ֣יךָ חָֽטְאוּ־ בָ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־ יַעֲשֶׂ֥ה אָדָ֖ם וְחָיָ֣ה בָהֶ֑ם וַיִּתְּנ֤וּ כָתֵף֙ סוֹרֶ֔רֶת וְעָרְפָּ֥ם הִקְשׁ֖וּ וְלֹ֥א שָׁמֵֽעוּ׃

passages.text: You were patient with them for many years, and Your Spirit admonished them through Your prophets. Yet they would not listen, so You gave them into the hands of the neighboring peoples.
passages.sermon:
God is patient and merciful.
God waited for His people for many years.
God warned them by His Spirit.
God spoke to them through His prophets.
The people did not listen to God.
God gave them into the hands of the neighboring nations.
passages.original: וַתִּמְשֹׁ֤ךְ עֲלֵיהֶם֙ שָׁנִ֣ים רַבּ֔וֹת וַתָּ֨עַד בָּ֧ם בְּרוּחֲךָ֛ בְּיַד־ נְבִיאֶ֖יךָ וְלֹ֣א הֶאֱזִ֑ינוּ וַֽתִּתְּנֵ֔ם בְּיַ֖ד עַמֵּ֥י הָאֲרָצֹֽת׃

passages.text: But in Your great compassion, You did not put an end to them; nor did You forsake them, for You are a gracious and compassionate God.
passages.sermon:
God is gracious and compassionate.
God has great compassion.
God did not destroy His people.
God did not abandon His people.
passages.original: וּֽבְרַחֲמֶ֧יךָ הָרַבִּ֛ים לֹֽא־ עֲשִׂיתָ֥ם כָּלָ֖ה וְלֹ֣א עֲזַבְתָּ֑ם כִּ֛י אֵֽל־ חַנּ֥וּן וְרַח֖וּם אָֽתָּה׃

passages.text: So now, our God, the great and mighty and awesome God who keeps His gracious covenant, do not view lightly all the hardship that has come upon us, and upon our kings and leaders, our priests and prophets, our ancestors and all Your people, from the days of the kings of Assyria until today.
passages.sermon:
Our God is great, mighty, and awesome.
God keeps His covenant and shows steadfast love.
God, do not ignore the hardship that has come upon us.
This hardship has come upon our kings.
It has come upon our leaders.
It has come upon our priests.
It has come upon our prophets.
It has come upon our ancestors.
It has come upon all Your people.
This hardship has lasted from the days of the kings of Assyria until today.
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֣ה אֱ֠לֹהֵינוּ הָאֵ֨ל הַגָּד֜וֹל הַגִּבּ֣וֹר וְהַנּוֹרָא֮ שׁוֹמֵ֣ר הַבְּרִ֣ית וְהַחֶסֶד֒ אַל־ יִמְעַ֣ט לְפָנֶ֡יךָ אֵ֣ת כָּל־ הַתְּלָאָ֣ה אֲֽשֶׁר־ מְ֠צָאַתְנוּ לִמְלָכֵ֨ינוּ לְשָׂרֵ֧ינוּ וּלְכֹהֲנֵ֛ינוּ וְלִנְבִיאֵ֥נוּ וְלַאֲבֹתֵ֖ינוּ וּלְכָל־ עַמֶּ֑ךָ מִימֵי֙ מַלְכֵ֣י אַשּׁ֔וּר עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: You are just in all that has befallen us, because You have acted faithfully, while we have acted wickedly.
passages.sermon:
God, You are just.
Everything that has happened to us is right.
You have always acted faithfully.
We have acted wickedly.
passages.original: וְאַתָּ֣ה צַדִּ֔יק עַ֖ל כָּל־ הַבָּ֣א עָלֵ֑ינוּ כִּֽי־ אֱמֶ֥ת עָשִׂ֖יתָ וַאֲנַ֥חְנוּ הִרְשָֽׁעְנוּ׃

passages.text: Our kings and leaders and priests and fathers did not obey Your law or listen to Your commandments and warnings that You gave them.
passages.sermon:
Our kings did not obey Your law.
Our leaders did not obey Your law.
Our priests did not obey Your law.
Our fathers did not obey Your law.
They did not listen to Your commandments.
They did not listen to Your warnings.
You gave these commandments and warnings to them.
passages.original: וְאֶת־ מְלָכֵ֤ינוּ שָׂרֵ֙ינוּ֙ כֹּהֲנֵ֣ינוּ וַאֲבֹתֵ֔ינוּ לֹ֥א עָשׂ֖וּ תּוֹרָתֶ֑ךָ וְלֹ֤א הִקְשִׁ֙יבוּ֙ אֶל־ מִצְוֺתֶ֔יךָ וּלְעֵ֣דְוֺתֶ֔יךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הַעִידֹ֖תָ בָּהֶֽם׃

passages.text: For even while they were in their kingdom, with the abundant goodness that You had given them, and in the spacious and fertile land that You had set before them, they would not serve You or turn from their wicked ways.
passages.sermon:
The people were in their own kingdom.
You had given them much goodness.
You set a spacious and fertile land before them.
They did not serve You.
They did not turn from their wicked ways.
passages.original: וְהֵ֣ם בְּמַלְכוּתָם֩ וּבְטוּבְךָ֨ הָרָ֜ב אֲשֶׁר־ נָתַ֣תָּ לָהֶ֗ם וּבְאֶ֨רֶץ הָרְחָבָ֧ה וְהַשְּׁמֵנָ֛ה אֲשֶׁר־ נָתַ֥תָּ לִפְנֵיהֶ֖ם לֹ֣א עֲבָד֑וּךָ וְֽלֹא־ שָׁ֔בוּ מִמַּֽעַלְלֵיהֶ֖ם הָרָעִֽים׃

passages.text: So here we are today as slaves in the land You gave our fathers to enjoy its fruit and goodness— here we are as slaves!
passages.sermon:
We are slaves today.
You gave this land to our fathers.
You gave it so they could eat its fruit.
You gave it so they could enjoy its goodness.
But now we are slaves in this land.
passages.original: הִנֵּ֛ה אֲנַ֥חְנוּ הַיּ֖וֹם עֲבָדִ֑ים וְהָאָ֜רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־ נָתַ֣תָּה לַאֲבֹתֵ֗ינוּ לֶאֱכֹ֤ל אֶת־ פִּרְיָהּ֙ וְאֶת־ טוּבָ֔הּ הִנֵּ֛ה אֲנַ֥חְנוּ עֲבָדִ֖ים עָלֶֽיהָ׃

passages.text: Its abundant harvest goes to the kings You have set over us because of our sins. And they rule over our bodies and our livestock as they please. We are in great distress.
passages.sermon:
God gave us a land with abundant harvest.
We sinned against God.
Because of our sins, God set kings over us.
These kings take the harvest from our land.
These kings rule over our bodies.
These kings rule over our livestock.
They do whatever they want with us and our animals.
We are in great distress.
passages.original: וּתְבוּאָתָ֣הּ מַרְבָּ֗ה לַמְּלָכִ֛ים אֲשֶׁר־ נָתַ֥תָּה עָלֵ֖ינוּ בְּחַטֹּאותֵ֑ינוּ וְעַ֣ל גְּ֠וִיֹּתֵינוּ מֹשְׁלִ֤ים וּבִבְהֶמְתֵּ֙נוּ֙ כִּרְצוֹנָ֔ם וּבְצָרָ֥ה גְדוֹלָ֖ה אֲנָֽחְנוּ׃פ

passages.text: In view of all this, we make a binding agreement, putting it in writing and sealing it with the names of our leaders, Levites, and priests.”
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel suffered as slaves in their own land.
They lost the freedom and blessings God gave their ancestors.
They saw that their sins brought this trouble.
They decided to act together.
They made a binding agreement.
They wrote this agreement down.
They sealed the agreement.
Their leaders, Levites, and priests put their names on the seal.
passages.original: וּבְכָל־ זֹ֕את אֲנַ֛חְנוּ כֹּרְתִ֥ים אֲמָנָ֖ה וְכֹתְבִ֑ים וְעַל֙ הֶֽחָת֔וּם שָׂרֵ֥ינוּ לְוִיֵּ֖נוּ כֹּהֲנֵֽינוּ׃
